panels.rationale: Single weight-bearing lateral radiograph demonstrating the captioned C sign, a characteristic radiographic manifestation of talocalcaneal coalition. The disease-focused review title identifies the subject as talocalcaneal coalition in children. [raw subtype: talocalcaneal]
panels.attribution_text: Zhou et al. Talocalcaneal coalition combined with flatfoot in children: diagnosis and treatment: a review.. Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research 2014. doi:10.1186/s13018-014-0129-9. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: The lateral X-ray image shows the C sign.
in_text_mentions: y of the sustentaculum in the lateral radiograph. The anatomic-pathologic results showed that the ‘C’ sign is a bony bridge between the talar dome and sustentaculum tali, in combination with a prominent inferior border of the sustentaculum tali (Figure 1). Brown et al. have shown that the ‘C’ sign may be more indicative of collapsing flatfoot deformity than coalition [26]. In addition, the fibula may come into contact with the lateral calcaneal wall during weight bearing and develop a pseudoarticulation in the presence of calcaneal valgus [19].Figure 1 The lateral X-ray image shows the C sign.
